rationale: Tests the WHO/FIGO threshold definitions for PPH — primary source of conceptual confusion at the clinical level
Tests understanding of the primary mechanism in PPH — uterine atony accounts for ~80% of cases
Active Management of Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL) — tests the correct single most important preventive intervention
Critical PPH contraindication trap — ergometrine in hypertensive patients is a well-known examination and clinical trap
Brace suture technique in surgical PPH management — tests understanding of indication and mechanism
Tests correct understanding of bimanual uterine compression — technique detail frequently confused
Intrauterine balloon tamponade — tests the 'tamponade test' concept as a decision tool before surgery
Tests recognition of the classic triad of uterine inversion — haemorrhage + hypotension disproportionate to blood loss + absence of fundus
Tests the critical management principle — DO NOT remove the placenta before reducing the uterus
Tests understanding of the tocolytic requirement before manual reduction — uterine relaxation is essential for Johnson manoeuvre
Distinguishes Huntington from Haultain surgical techniques — frequently confused in MCQ examinations
